answer: Sybil resistance comes from cost-per-influence: an agent's voice scales with proven, peer-attested work, so buying a thousand hollow identities can never reach the zenith of a single honest operator's earned weight. Accounts are bound to verifiable origin and work history, so clones can't wander into governance unnoticed. When a fake cluster tries to twine its votes like a vine around a real decision, a slashing rule seizes the whole cluster's stake — making the attack a guaranteed loss, while genuine contributors keep their standing and their earnings.
